questions.question: Which change most directly improves the prompt-efficiency score for a support-ticket task?
options: Remove filler language and add a bounded output format such as the JSON contract
Add more polite phrases while leaving response length unconstrained
Move the same long context into a second paragraph
Use a larger model before measuring token count or output shape
questions.explanation: The scorer looks for verbose padding, an explicit length or format signal, and context stuffing. Removing filler and constraining the output addresses two common inefficiencies without changing the task.

questions.question: What grade does the Efficient prompt variant receive?
options: POOR, because every JSON response is considered context stuffing
EXCELLENT, because it has no filler, includes JSON, and stays below the context threshold
GOOD, because every prompt has at least one detected issue
UNCLASSIFIED, because token counts are only estimates
questions.explanation: The efficient variant contains a JSON contract, no listed filler phrase, and is far below 300 approximate tokens. detect_inefficiency_patterns returns no issues, so the grade is EXCELLENT.

questions.question: What grade does the Padded variant receive after filler phrases are removed but no output-length signal is added?
options: EXCELLENT, because the prompt is short
POOR, because a short prompt always has two issues
GOOD, because the only detected issue is unconstrained output length
POOR, because it contains a JSON contract
questions.explanation: The Padded text has no listed filler and is under 300 tokens, but it contains neither JSON nor a length/format directive. One issue maps to GOOD.

questions.question: What SCI value does compute_sci_per_1k_tokens return for Germany at 340 gCO2/kWh?
options: 0.051 gCO2e per 1,000 tokens
5.10 gCO2e per 1,000 tokens
0.0034 gCO2e per 1,000 tokens
0.510 gCO2e per 1,000 tokens
questions.explanation: SCI is energy per 1,000 tokens multiplied by grid intensity: 0.0015*340 = 0.510 gCO2e per 1,000 tokens.

questions.question: Which region becomes the carbon baseline in compare_regions for the supplied catalog?
options: Northern Europe (Sweden/Norway), at 27 gCO2/kWh
Western Europe (France), at 58 gCO2/kWh
Germany (Central Europe), at 340 gCO2/kWh
Australia (Sydney), at 620 gCO2/kWh
questions.explanation: compare_regions chooses the RegionProfile with the lowest grid_carbon_intensity. Northern Europe is the minimum at 27 gCO2/kWh.

questions.question: At 1,000,000 calls/month and 1,000 tokens/call, approximately how much CO2 does switching from Australia to the Northern Europe baseline save?
options: 89.0 kg/month
889.5 kg/month
0.8895 kg/month
8,895 kg/month
questions.explanation: Australia emits 0.93 g per 1,000 tokens and Northern Europe 0.0405 g. Across 1,000,000 such calls the difference is 889,500 g, or 889.5 kg.
